items.title: Resolving temporal threat uncertainty by observational learning involves the amygdala, hippocampus and anterior insula
items.summary: Abstract By observing others’ experiences, humans learn about threats while avoiding firsthand dangers. In firsthand learning, temporally predictable and unpredictable threats can be mechanistically discerned. items.summary: Understanding the structural connectivity of the human brain during fetal life is essential for uncovering the early foundations of neural function and vulnerability to developmental disorders. items.title: The challenge of out-of-distribution detection in motor imagery BCIs
items.summary: Objective Machine Learning classifiers used in Brain-Computer Interfaces make classifications based on the distribution of examples on which they were trained. When exposed to EEG from unfamiliar classes they can only make blind guesses. Instead of allowing such guesses, these Out-of-Distribution (OOD) samples should be detected and rejected to improve the robustness of BCIs against unfamiliar cognitive states. items.title: Spatial learning strengthens hippocampal but not prefrontal influence on nucleus reuniens in rats

items.title: The Structure of Yearning: Bouzid's Rule (B+F=Nf) as an Axiological Framework for Virtue and Vice
items.summary: Contemporary debates in the axiology of theism evaluate spiritual yearning based on its object (theistic, ultimate, or secular) or its quantity (moderate vs. excessive). items.title: Reimagining the past: Historical imagination in theory and practice
items.summary: Historical imagination is not merely an auxiliary tool in historical understanding but its constitutive condition—a claim articulated consistently across Collingwood’s re-enactment, Dilthey’s Verstehen, and Gadamer’s fusion of horizons, and supported by cognitive neuroscience. Yet despite this foundational status, historical imagination remains conceptually under-specified in history education research, and the empirical work documenting its importance has not provided a theoretical account of why affect is constitutive of historical understanding or how it operates. items.title: Neural dynamical systems on ferroelectric compute-in-memory for real-time forecasting
items.summary: Abstract Neural dynamical systems are expressive temporal predictors that capture continuous-time dynamics through fine-grained state updates. However, this sequential structure maps poorly onto digital hardware optimized for dense matrix operations, a mismatch that analog neuromorphic computing, with its native continuous-time dynamics, can resolve. We introduce FerroNDS, a neuromorphic system built from two analog primitives: an integrator for temporal accumulation and an oscillator for frequency-selective filtering. items.title: Dissociable Intrinsic Connectivity Networks for Salience Processing and Executive Control
items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. Here, we used task-free connectivity analyses to isolate and characterize two distinct networks typically coactivated during functional MRI tasks. We identified a "salience network," anchored by dorsal anterior cingulate (dACC) and orbital frontoinsular cortices with robust connectivity to subcortical and limbic structures, and an "executive-control network" that links dorsolateral frontal and parietal neocortices. items.title: Polyneuropathy secondary to nitrous oxide misuse in a case at the Ibrahima Pierre NDIAYE neuroscience clinic, at the Fann national university hospital center
items.summary: Recreational misuse of nitrous oxide, a laughing gas, has increased sharply among young adults in recent years. This misuse can lead to multiple complications affecting several organs, including the central and peripheral nervous systems. Spinal cord and peripheral nervous system disorders are among the neurological complications most often due to vitamin B12 deficiency.
